description:
Cortes Island is a jewel to explore. White sand beaches, temperate rainforests, and views from rocky bluffs offer a myriad of recreational opportunities.

The island is 25 km long and 13 km wide. A year-round population of about a thousand residents lives in the communities of Whaletown, Gorge Harbour, Squirrel Cove, and Mansons Landing. Klahoose Village in Squirrel Cove is a home for island's First Nations.

The population changes with seasons as summer brings a lot of visitors to the island.

We respectfully acknowledge the Klahoose, Tla'amin and Homalco Nations upon whose territories the  programs and activities of the Cortes Island Museum & Archives take place.

Photo credits: Melanie Boyle, Gary Fast, Peter Jackel, Grazyna Trzesicka, Alex Woywitka, and others.  A few pictures come from the Museum Archives.

(Release 2026/10/29)

The parks and trails of Cortes Island help preserve our precious wilderness areas while providing access to places of incredible beauty. Spend your time hiking through our peaceful, cool green forests. Pack a lunch and enjoy the spectacular views from Hank's Beach, Green Mountain, or Easter Bluff.

To help protect our natural spaces and wildlife, follow these rules:

- Stay on trails
- Keep pets on a leash and clean up after them
- Pack out what you packed in
- Build fires only in designated areas when no fire bans are in effect
- Extinguish fires thoroughly
- Camp only in designated areas

Please respect private properties adjacent to trail systems!

For your safety, stay off trails during high winds, as there is a danger of falling branches and trees.

You have a few options for camping on Cortes Island. Most campgrounds are booked well before the season, so call in advance if you plan to camp on Cortes Island.

Most provincial parks and conservation areas do not have camping areas, and camping is prohibited in these parks.

Docks on Cortes Island first appeared around 125 years ago to support steamships and the commercial fishing industry. Today, the Harbour Authority of Cortes Island oversees five Community Docks in Cortes Bay, Squirrel Cove, Gorge Harbour, Mansons Landing, and Whaletown.

All docks provide safe, well-maintained moorage year-round for a variety of marine users.

Except for the Cortes Bay location, each dock is surrounded by a small community that offers services, attractions, and activities.

For information about assured transient docking reservations, visit CortesHarbours.ca.

Red pins mark full docks.
Blue pins mark beach and ocean access points for launching small boats or kayaks.

Cortes has three beautiful ocean beaches and one sandy lake beach located in Mansons Landing Park at Hague Lake.

A few water access points allow you to reach the ocean shore, and some are suitable for launching canoes and kayaks.

Cortes Island offers a variety of accommodations to meet each visitor's needs including campgrounds, wilderness tenting, private cabins for rent, a motel, and B&Bs. 

For options not visible on the map, we recommend checking Tideline, our community website at www.cortesisland.com, as well as your favourite vacation rental platforms.

Cortes has three grocery stores open year-round and some seasonal places to eat.

All grocery stores offer coffee and snacks and have a place to sit and relax. Additionally, a few seasonal takeout outlets are open during summer, with locations that may vary from season to season.

For a meal, consider takeout, visit a local grocery store, or dine at the Hollyhock restaurant for more refined dining, where reservations are required.

Most places too eat are located in downtown Manson's so enlarge the area around Manson' to see all described options.

Cortes has four grocery stores open year-round. All stores offer coffee and snacks, and most have space to sit and relax. Most also sell local crafts and gifts.

Cortes Market, Squirrel Cove, and the Gorge stores each have a hardware section stocked with basic light bulbs, nails, simple tools, electrical and plumbing supplies, and seasonal garden items.

Red markers indicate grocery stores.
Blue markers indicate other stores.

From the time of the Coast Salish people to the present, Cortes Island has been home to those who value their cultural practices and diverse art forms.

The Island still attracts historians, philosophers, writers, musicians, artists and craftspeople who enjoy sharing their knowledge, skills and creations with others.

Beyond beaches, forests, and hiking trails, Cortes offers a variety of recreational areas. 

From playgrounds and a pickleball court to a skateboard park, Cortes Island offers activities for all ages.

Many playgrounds are located in the Manson's area so enlarge the map to see all options described.

Cortes Island has one junior primary school, three community halls, a radio station, and several organizations committed to the people and environment of Cortes Island. 

Most of these organizations do not have a designated map point. 

If you are interested in these organizations, please talk to the museum host.

Today, three operational post offices remain on Cortes Island.

Historically, a few other locations served small communities when road access around the island was poor or non-existent. Mail arrived by steamship, plane, or ferry. Mail days were occasions to meet neighbours and socialize. 

In the museum library, you can find three books by Peter Smith with postal history of Discovery Islands.

Red pin indicates operational post office (currently, three locations).
Blue pin indicates historical location.

Cortes Island offers essential services including Emergency Services, Cortes Health Centre, Visitor Information Booth, Vancouver Island Regional Library, two gas/propane filling stations, electrical charging stations for cars and e-bikes, recycling centre, and public washrooms.

Emergency services for police, ambulance and fire are available 24 hours a day by dialing 911. 

The BC Ambulance Station is located in Mansons Landing, Firehall 1. If necessary, ambulance crews will evacuate patients via helicopter, Coast Guard or ferry. Firehall 2 is located in Whaletown. The Police/RCMP are located on Quadra Island but respond as required.

Volunteer firefighters provide firefighting, medical first responder, auto extrication, and fire prevention services as part of their core responsibilities.

Public washrooms include flush and pit toilets. See dedicated map to find out the locations.

Public washrooms are found in each park; they are typically pit toilets. You can also find public washrooms in some stores and public places during their open hours.

The locations marked on the map are generally open at all times unless otherwise indicated.

Red pins are flush toilets.
Blue pins are pit toilets.

Logging on Cortes Island began in the late 1800s. It was carried out by Europeans, with some help from Chinese, Japanese, and local Klahoose crews. The first logger was Moses Cross Ireland, who logged around Cortes towards Carrington Bay -- possibly also Green Valley -- before moving on to what was called Camp Island, now the Subtle Islands. Early hand-loggers harvested large timber using springboards, crosscut saws ("misery whips"), oxen, and floating camps.

Today, almost no original forest remains on the island. Some lots are still owned by Mosaic. Sustainable logging is mostly carried on by the Cortes Forestry General Partnership (CFGP), an equal partnership between the Klahoose Forestry N0 2 Limited Partnership (KF2LP) and the Cortes Community Forest Cooperative (CCFC) committed to building a resilient and vibrant world-class community-based forestry operation on Cortes Island.

A few large trees remain here and there. When you get to any of them, stop and reflect on the past, present and future.
